title: Runtime bench corral: deterministic workload catalog, stability windows, and CI performance guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket builds a 'bench corral' — a consolidated harness and artifact format for deterministic workload runs across kernel variants, attention optimizations, and prefill/decode schedules. The goal is to produce stable, reproducible baselines that CI can compare against with quantitative guardrails (not just mean token time).

Background and motivation:
- Current benchmark outputs are noisy across machines and kernel combinations; root-cause analysis is slow because artifacts are scattered and formats vary.
- We need a single manifest and runner that can: 1) run deterministic seeds for stochastic workloads, 2) emit histogram + KV cache metrics, 3) record active kernel selection/context for each token range, and 4) produce delta artifacts used by CI gates.

What this ticket will deliver:
- A workload catalog manifest format (bench-corral.manifest.json) that declares: model, sequence distribution, prompt corpus, deterministic seed, kernel routing matrix, attention flags, prefill/decode pacing, and expected stability window.
- A runner that performs shadow runs (production traffic replay) and synthetic runs (seeded), and emits: token-level latency histogram (p50/p90/p95/p99), memory footprint over time, kernel-selection trace, and KV prefix hit/miss counts.
- A deterministic-stability pipeline that compares new run artifacts to the golden baseline using: 1) quantile delta thresholds, 2) noise-floor characterization, and 3) automatic severity labeling (info/warn/fail).
- CI perf gate integration: on PR, run a trimmed subset of the manifest (fast-path seeds) and require no regressions beyond defined thresholds; failures produce a triage artifact with kernel-selection diffs and suggested rollback toggles.
- Backwards-compatible exporter so existing benchmark dashboards ingest corral artifacts.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not rework kernel implementations themselves; it is focused on harness, artifacts, and gating.
- It will not replace long-running golden suites (those remain for scheduled full-regression runs).

High-level plan / milestones:
1) Spec and manifest format (week 1) — agreed JSON schema and example manifests for three representative workloads (short-chat, long-context-code, embedding-batch).
2) Runner + trace capture (week 2) — capture token-level kernel selector and latency histograms; lightweight synthetic runner for CI.
3) Diff engine and threshold rules (week 3) — quantile comparisons, noise floor estimation, and severity mapping.
4) CI integration and test PR (week 4) — wire into GitHub Actions for runtime repo and add gating logic.
5) Dashboard ingest and rollout (week 5) — hook into existing perf dashboards and announce rollout.

Operational notes:
- Use existing KR telemetry proto where possible; add minimal fields for kernel id and kernel-version.
- Keep synthetic runs small (<=50 seeds) for PRs; full corral runs gated to nightly clusters.
- Provide toggles in the console for temporarily disabling specific kernel variants during an incident (runbook integration).

Risks and mitigations:
- Flaky hardware can create false positives: mitigate by running 3 repeat seeds and using median-of-medians to estimate the noise floor.
- Large artifact sizes: compress histograms and store deltas only for CI artifacts; full artifacts go to long-term storage.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest JSON schema documented and 3 example manifests checked into runtime-perf-bench repo
Runner produces per-token latency histograms, kernel-selection trace, and KV cache metrics for synthetic and shadow runs
Diff engine outputs a human-readable triage artifact highlighting quantile regressions and kernel-selection changes
CI job added: PRs run a fast-corral subset and fail if p95 or p99 regress beyond configured thresholds
Perf dashboard ingests corral artifacts and displays delta summaries alongside existing baselines
comments: 2026-02-10 Aisha Patel: Created initial spec and wireframe for manifest schema. Put example manifests for short-chat / long-code / embed-batch in /docs/bench-corral/examples.

2026-02-13 Marcus Huang: Spike complete — prototype runner captures kernel id at token granularity. Observed systematic p99 uplift when prefilling with attention-optimized kernel B on long-code workload. Captured artifacts: gs://redwood-bench/corral/spikes/ENG-25123/.

2026-02-16 Lina Gómez (review): Reviewed manifest schema. Suggested adding 'stability_window_ms' field per-workload and a 'seed_repeats' parameter for noise estimation. Also requested explicit 'hardware_hint' to avoid cross-hardware comparisons.
2026-02-20 Omar Farouk: Implemented baseline diff engine and added quantile thresholds config. Drafted severity mapping: <2% p95 delta = info, 2-6% = warn, >6% = fail. Needs team sign-off.

2026-02-25 Marcus Huang: CI job added to runtime repo (circle -> GH Actions migration). Fast-corral run uses 12 seeds, checks p90/p95/p99. Example failing PR captured triage artifact and linked kernel-selection toggle in the report. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4256

2026-03-01 Aisha Patel: Decision: Use median-of-3 repeats for CI to reduce false positives. Follow-up: add automated rerun-on-flaky-hardware step to CI job. Planning to merge runner + diff engine by 2026-03-10.
